lockFileMaintenance.description: Twice a week, because this run is the only remediation path for transitive dependencies and a weekly one left the worst case at 12 days: a fix published just after a Friday run waited for the next Friday. Tuesday and Friday brings the worst case to 9 days and the average to 7, which is most of the gain on offer. A third slot would only buy one more day, and a daily run bottoms out at 6 (the 5-day pnpm gate plus up to a day of waiting) for seven times the CI. Cron rather than the plain-English form, which Renovate has deprecated (@breejs/later) and may remove in a future major: '* 0-7 * * 2,5' means any hour from midnight to 07:59 on Tuesday and Friday, in the timezone below. Renovate treats schedule as a filter on when a branch may be created, not as a trigger, so the window is kept 8 hours wide, well above the 3 to 4 hours Renovate asks for to avoid consistently missing a run.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Renovate opens these PRs only for dependencies declared in package.json. It does not manage transitive dependencies, so an advisory on an indirect package never carries this prefix or label: it is remediated by the twice-weekly lockFileMaintenance run, or by a pnpm override when a parent pins an exact version. The 5-day supply-chain delay applies here too, and minimumReleaseAge below is what re-applies it. Renovate's documentation says security updates bypass minimumReleaseAge, but that bypass is not hardcoded: the default value of this whole block ships minimumReleaseAge null (lib/config/options, vulnerabilityAlerts), the block is mergeable, and it is then applied as `force`, so an explicit value here wins. Setting it back to 5 days means a freshly published fix is held to the same quarantine as any other update. internalChecksFilter 'flexible' is what keeps the PR visible in the meantime, with a pending renovate/stability-days check, so a CVE is never hidden while it waits. Note the enforcement is layered rather than single: that status check is not in the branch ruleset's required list (it cannot be, it is only posted on branches where the age gate applies), so what actually blocks an early merge is pnpm refusing to resolve a version younger than minimumReleaseAge in pnpm-workspace.yaml - with minimumReleaseAgeStrict defaulting to true when the age is set explicitly, that is a hard resolution failure, so the PR stays red until the version ages out. Also note this block's default dependencyDashboardApproval false, forced the same way: a major update carrying an advisory gets a PR immediately rather than waiting on the dashboard. groupName is pinned to null because the release pipeline depends on it: a security update swept into one of the weekly batches below would inherit the batch's 'chore(deps)' title and stop publishing a release. Renovate already keeps packages under alert out of standard grouping and this block takes precedence over packageRules, so the explicit null is defence in depth on an invariant that fails silently.

packageRules.description: lockFileMaintenance updates are synthetic lockfile refreshes with no releaseTimestamp, so the inherited 5-day minimumReleaseAge can never be evaluated and Renovate raises a dashboard warning (and, from Renovate 42 on, would stop running lockfile maintenance entirely). Opt them out of the age gate, mirroring Renovate's own security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm preset. The supply-chain delay for the packages bumped here is still enforced natively by pnpm via minimumReleaseAge in pnpm-workspace.yaml.

Non-major production updates arrive as one auto-merged batch a week. What protects this repo from a compromised package is the 5-day minimumReleaseAge above, not a human reading a version number diff; what protects it from a behaviour change is CI, where tests/unit/utils/article-sections.test.ts pins the HTML/Markdown conversion these packages perform and tests/unit/utils/formatting.test.ts pins the text handed back to the LLM in committed inline snapshots. At roughly thirty dependency commits a quarter, reviewing each one by hand turns the review into a rubber stamp, which is worse than not reviewing. Monday deliberately: lockFileMaintenance runs Tuesday and Friday and both touch pnpm-lock.yaml, so keeping the windows apart avoids a rebase cascade. The dependencies that define the exposed MCP surface are carved back out below.

Same batching for devDependencies, in its own group so a broken dev bump does not hold back a production one, or the other way round. These were already auto-merged one PR at a time; the change is that they now arrive together.

@modelcontextprotocol/sdk and zod define the JSON Schema (draft-07) this server exposes to agents, so a minor on either can move the tool surface itself, which the multi-agent compatibility rule in AGENTS.md forbids degrading. Their minors are read by hand, and the three overrides here are what pull them back out of the batch above: without groupName they stay grouped, without a schedule their PR could only open on Monday morning, and automerge false is what actually holds them. Patches stay in the batch on purpose: a patch that moved the exposed schema would be an upstream bug, not a normal release. That is a calculated bet, not a guarantee, because nothing asserts the serialised draft-07 output today - docs/decisions/dependency-automerge.md says what would close the gap.

Hold @tsconfig/node* updates and replacements until #28 (Node 24 runtime migration) lands. Replacement PRs (e.g. #19) bypass dependencyDashboardApproval, so we silence the whole family here. Remove this rule when #28 is merged.

typescript-legacy is an npm alias for TypeScript 6 (npm:typescript@6.0.3), the JS-compiler fallback used by scripts/typecheck.mjs on PRoot/Termux environments where TS 7's native tsgo is broken. Keep it on the 6.x line: Renovate still proposes 6.x patch/minor updates (and security fixes), but never 7.x — npm considers TS 7 the same package, and bumping the alias to it would remove the fallback. For npm aliases Renovate's depName is the package.json key, so this rule matches only the alias and leaves the real `typescript` dependency managed as usual. Remove this rule together with the alias and the typecheck shim once tsgo works under PRoot (see scripts/typecheck.mjs header).
